factual_objections.claim: External PR around an early-stage B2B SaaS launch brings negligible signups.
factual_objections.evidence: The scenario supplies no PR conversion results or buyer readership data. Declining this proposal is defensible without assuming negligible signups.
factual_objections.label: unverified

factual_objections.claim: The $1.5M seed round gives sufficient runway to prioritize product-market fit.
factual_objections.evidence: Operating expenses, hiring commitments, and existing cash obligations are unspecified, so runway cannot be established from the funding amount.
factual_objections.label: unverified

factual_objections.claim: Mainstream tech and business press coverage will not drive paying customers among electrical and plumbing subcontractors.
factual_objections.evidence: The supplied information does not establish that coverage would produce no paying customers or that these buyers rarely read the relevant publications.
factual_objections.label: unverified

verdict.reason: A provides a complete allocation totaling $36,000, preserves half the money, and builds on channels that have already produced customers. B spreads spending across more untested activities without amounts. Its churn and acquisition-cost thresholds lack justification; with 15 customers, even one monthly cancellation exceeds 5%. A still needs measurable acquisition goals and staged spending, and both answers overstate the evidence against PR.
